records.text: The Lich King presents himself as the source of his chosen death knights' immortality and casts them as instruments of vengeance. He directs their attention against the Scarlet Crusade at Light's Hope and New Avalon, then declares that the Argent Dawn will face the Scourge's reprisal. His orders treat resistance as a challenge to Scourge power.
Prince Keleseth is an undead prince.

Instructor Razuvious trains death knights in the Heart of Acherus. He teaches runeforging and presents the initiate’s hunger as a trial of survival, making an unworthy captive fight for freedom. His praise celebrates a champion in service to the Lich King, whose purpose is to sow chaos and destruction.

At Death’s Breach, Prince Valanar directs the Scourge’s campaign against the Scarlet Crusade through terror, slaughter, and tactical attacks. He treats death knights as weapons for the Lich King’s war, takes macabre pleasure in the scent of fresh Crusader corpses, and expects personal commendation for destroying the Scarlet fleet.
The Acherus Necromancers are Scourge spellcasters who answer an instructor and raise minions to feast upon the weak. Their brief spoken replies show dutiful obedience.
A humanoid Scarlet Crusade prisoner in the Plaguelands' Scarlet Enclave.
A humanoid Argent Dawn prisoner in the Plaguelands' Scarlet Enclave.
A humanoid Death Knight Initiate.

Once dead and now reborn, this initiate addresses Arthas as king and says he has returned only to serve his master. His broken recollection and reverence frame him as a newly raised servant whose loyalty centers on Arthas.
A humanoid Death Knight Initiate.
A humanoid death knight initiate in the Scarlet Enclave.

Distressed and confused, this initiate asks where he is and who he has become, then begs for an end to unbearable pain. His words convey a mind struggling with its present state rather than confident allegiance.
The recorded challenge exchange gives this initiate a brash, taunting manner: they boast about owning an opponent, threaten to tear out their heart, and shout “No potions!” during the encounter.

Highlord Darion Mograine directs the Scourge campaign against the Scarlet forces, sending death knights to lead the march on New Avalon. He treats the Lich King's will as a command shared by death knights and submits to it himself. The destruction of the Scarlet fleet impresses him, briefly recalling his father before he dismisses the thought.
Baron Rivendare is an undead baron.
Fury is an undead in the Scarlet Enclave.
Koltira Deathweaver is an undead in the Scarlet Enclave.
Orbaz Bloodbane is an undead in the Scarlet Enclave.
Thassarian is an undead in the Scarlet Enclave.

Lady Alistra is a Death Knight trainer in the Hall of Command, teaching its school of unholy. Her words cast unholy power as a means to command death. The conversation also presents options for training and unlearning talents.

Lord Thorval identifies himself as headmaster of the Hall of Command’s blood school, one of three dark arts taught there. His lessons describe blood as a weapon and stolen energy as a way to endure seemingly endless battle; the conversation includes training and talent options.

Amal'thazad is the arch-lich who holds dominion over frost among the Hall of Command’s three Death Knight schools, according to Lord Thorval. Amal'thazad’s own words evoke icy despair and death, and the conversation presents an option to seek training.
A Val'kyr Battle-maiden, an undead val'kyr warrior.
An enslaved laborer is a worker forced into labor.
A mindless laborer is a worker whose designation marks it as lacking reason.

Scourge Commander Thalanor is an officer at Ebon Hold who arranges gryphon transport to Death's Breach for arriving death knights. He speaks with gleeful, violent zeal, promising that they will herald chaos, death, and destruction.
A Scarlet Crusade fighter stationed at New Avalon, this crusader fights the Scourge and calls its enemies demons. Those battle cries show the Crusader's severe religious framing of the conflict.
A Scarlet Crusade commander stationed at New Avalon, distinguished from its rank-and-file fighters by command rank.

High General Abbendis speaks for crusaders seeking to reclaim New Avalon and burn Scourge in their way. She ties permission to remain there to inquisitors' judgment of one's devotion to the Light, insisting the Light remains strong among the pure. She urges her side to fight and push back.
Shely bears the rank of captain.
Street bears the title of bishop.
Goodman bears the designation Blacksmith.
Kaleiki bears the title of foreman.
Zierhut bears the designation Lead Cannonneer.
Torturer LeCraft is a humanoid in the Scarlet Enclave.
Stable Master Mercer is a humanoid in the Scarlet Enclave.
Commander Jordan is a commander in the Scarlet Enclave.

Scarlet Peasant speaks in frightened, pleading excuses: he cites a sick grandmother and five children, insists nobody needs to die, begs for mercy, and offers obedience. Other lines add comic embarrassment and regret about quitting drinking.
High Abbot Landgren is a humanoid. He asks, “But none of you could possibly have anything to worry about, right?” in a tone of wry reassurance directed at a group.
A citizen of New Avalon.
A humanoid citizen of New Avalon in the Scarlet Enclave.

A Havenshire resident, this citizen meets death knights with defiance but also begs to be spared and promises to flee. They fear their children will be orphaned, giving their struggle for freedom a family stake.

A Havenshire resident, this citizen meets death knights with defiance but also begs to be spared and promises to flee. They fear their children will be orphaned, giving their struggle for freedom a family stake.
A Scarlet Preacher. Noth the Plaguebringer wants Crusader Skulls like those Scarlet Preachers carry for his plague cauldron work.
A Havenshire stallion, a riding horse that gives a soft “Brr...” once its rider has gone.
A Havenshire mare, a riding horse that gives a soft “Brrr..” once its rider has gone.
A Havenshire colt used for passenger travel. It gives a brief “Brr...” and reacts when its passenger dismounts.
A Scarlet medic who voices confidence in the Crusade’s victory and calls for purging. It denounces outsiders as monsters, revealing a hostile, zealous stance.
A Scarlet infantryman who voices confidence in the Crusade’s victory and calls for purging. It denounces outsiders as monsters, showing the hostility behind its martial role.
A Scarlet marksman who warns outsiders away and calls for purging; its appeal to the Light frames that hostility as cleansing. Its combat training includes a close-range strike.
A Scarlet captain who voices confidence in the Crusade’s victory and calls for purging. It denounces outsiders as monsters and uses ranged fire, pairing an officer’s title with active combat.
A Scarlet Gryphon in the Scarlet Enclave.
The Scourge Sky Darkener is a combat construct deployed against people fleeing Havenshire. It uses Sky Darkener Assault, and the Sky Darkeners' saronite arrows target those fleeing for New Avalon.

Orithos the Sky Darkener is stationed at Death's Breach. Orithos directs recovery of scarce saronite arrows for the Sky Darkeners, described as constructs targeting people fleeing Havenshire for New Avalon; the arrows may land near Havenshire Farm. This work feeds the Scourge war machine.

Salanar the Horseman challenges death knights to steal a Havenshire horse and prove mastery over an unbound charger. Salanar offers to transform the stolen horse into a deathcharger, then invites the rider to enter the Realm of Shadows, defeat a dark rider and claim the raised charger. Success earns Salanar's praise, and the Horseman's Call can summon Salanar back to Death's Breach.

Gothik the Harvester is a grand necromancer of the Lich King who says he came from Naxxramas to feast on souls and fight the Scarlet forces. At Death’s Breach he offers a plague device to turn Scarlet miners into ghouls, and addresses them with contemptuous threats; his dry aside about old habits hints at a practiced, sardonic manner.

This unnamed Havenshire citizen is among people displaced by the Scarlet Crusade’s seizure of the area. The citizen fears losing family and having nowhere to stay, and angrily challenges Abbendis over the Light’s failure to protect them. The lines give this speaker a grief-stricken, accusatory voice within the crowd.

This unnamed Havenshire citizen mourns the loss of home and family amid the Crusade’s takeover. The speaker says the Light failed to save a wife and children, laments that the stables and mill stand abandoned, and fears for the horses. Their words convey bereavement, anger at the Light, and concern for what remains of the community.

Stable Master Kitrik is fiercely protective of his horses and furious about repeated thefts. He insults suspected thieves, threatens to send them back to the Lich King in pieces, and warns them that they will face the gallows. His replies after an apparent reprimand remain blunt and mocking.
An Acherus geist is a humanoid creature whose brief, broken speech shows a keen interest in shiny things.
Hargus the Gimp sells supplies, greeting buyers with “Come to buy from Hargus, you have?”
Known as the Lich King.
Scarlet Farm Hounds are beasts associated with farm life in the Scarlet area.
Shadowy Tormentors are elemental foes found across several parts of the region. Their name marks them as shadowy tormentors, and their presence spans the surrounding area.
An Acherus Deathcharger, a steed that rears up to beckon a rider. Once its rider dismounts, it soon departs.
A Plague Spreader in the Plaguelands: The Scarlet Enclave.
A Scarlet Miner works among the Scarlet workforce in the local mine sites. This entry is represented across several nearby areas, as one of many workers sharing the mining role.
A Scarlet Miner works among the Scarlet workforce in the local mine sites. This entry appears across a smaller set of nearby areas, as one worker in the wider mining operation.
A Scarlet Cannon is a functional siege weapon in the local Scarlet area, with a direct interaction available.
A Scarlet Fleet Defender is a combatant stationed in the fleet’s zone.
A Scarlet Land Cannon, a fixed gun in the Scarlet fleet area that fires cannonballs at foes.
A Scarlet Fleet Guardian is a combatant stationed in the Scarlet fleet area.
A Scarlet Fleet Guardian is a combatant stationed in the Scarlet fleet area.
A Scarlet Land Cannon is a combat unit found in the Scarlet fleet area.
A Scarlet Fleet Defender, a soldier of the Scarlet Fleet stationed in the Scarlet Enclave.
Scarlet Cannon is an artillery piece positioned among Scarlet forces in the Scarlet Enclave.
A necromancer associated by name with Acherus, found in the Scarlet Enclave. Its title gives it a necromantic role.

Gothik the Harvester is a Scourge figure working in the Scarlet Enclave. He urges a beast to rise and fly for the Scourge and examines corpses for what they may yield. When geists interfere with the bodies, he curses them and orders them away, showing contempt for scavengers and a practical interest in usable remains.
Scarlet miners are laborers of the Scarlet forces in the Scarlet Enclave; this example appears across several local areas.
A Scarlet peasant is a common laborer found in several the Scarlet Enclave areas.
A Scarlet Gryphon, a gryphon in the service of the Scarlet forces.
A Scarlet Medic is a healer serving the Scarlet forces.
A Scarlet Infantryman, a foot soldier among the Scarlet forces.
A Scarlet Captain, an officer among the Scarlet forces.
An Acherus Deathcharger is a deathcharger associated with Acherus.
A Scourge Plaguehound is a plaguehound serving the Scourge.
An undead Gluttonous Geist in the Scarlet Enclave.

Prince Valanar is a Scourge prince who urges death knights to heed the Lich King's words and celebrates the Scourge's campaign against the Scarlet Crusade. He treats fallen enemies as fuel for the growing host and proclaims the Scourge's gains at New Avalon and the coast, presenting conquest as a source of expanding strength.
Salanar the Horseman addresses a death knight with approval, praising the glory their actions have brought to the Scourge. His line presents him as a voice of Scourge approval.
An undead Dark Rider of Acherus in the Scarlet Enclave.

Baron Rivendare directs Scourge attacks on New Avalon, ordering the deaths of Scarlet Crusaders and citizens. He says he enjoys the Scourge’s recurring battles with the Crusade, which he regards as irrational and heedless of human life. He serves the Lich King and invites an effective death knight to become his minion, joking that Stratholme needs a mayor.

Prince Keleseth calls himself the blood lord, ruler of southeastern Northrend, and gladly serves the Lich King for souls to sate his thirst. He uses pointed “persuaders” to extract information from Scarlet soldiers and seeks their registry to trace their movements and investigate the “Crimson Dawn.” His replies urge using the weapons until a captive breaks.

Koltira Deathweaver is a Scourge death knight badly wounded in the fight against the Scarlet Crusade, though he still urges others to strike back and free prisoners. He resents Thassarian's attempt to rescue him, calling it a breach of their order's covenants and his friend a blasted fool.

Thassarian is a Scourge death knight who considers Koltira one of their best and refuses to give up hope that he survived captivity. Their bond reflects Thassarian's broader view that death has made former enemies into brothers among the Scourge; he also directs vengeance against the Scarlet Crusade.

Orbaz Bloodbane is a Scourge death knight who directs efforts against the Scarlet Crusade around New Avalon. He is calculating and ruthless: he extracts patrol information, arranges an undercover courier operation, and turns quickly from one lead to the threat of the encroaching armies. His remarks to Thassarian show a hard creed that only the strong should survive, contempt for newer death knights, and personal hostility toward his fellow knight.

Noth the Plaguebringer is a Scourge plague specialist tasked with preparing a cauldron for New Avalon. He speaks with cutting impatience, insulting a death knight's intelligence while explaining what he needs, then matter-of-factly describes the cauldron's plague as deadly to the living and empowering to the Scourge.
A Death Knight among the Acherus population.
A death knight serving in Acherus, armed with frost magic such as Icy Touch.
A Scarlet Commander of the Crusade, hostile to Scourge intruders and devoted to cleansing them by the Light. Its battle cries demand a purging and proclaim the Crusade's victory.
A Crypt Guardian stationed in Acherus crypt areas.

A Scarlet Preacher of the Crusade, voicing calls to cleanse and kill Scourge enemies and proclaiming the Crusade's victory. Under interrogation, the preacher says the High General decides who may leave or stay, and describes Crimson Dawn as an awakening set in motion before outsiders came, with followers doing as they are told.
A Scarlet Crusader who treats intruders as monsters and invokes the Light and purging in combat. Its battle cries express a zealous, hostile stance toward outsiders.

An unnamed citizen of New Avalon facing mortal danger and the loss of family. This citizen resists surrender, condemns the army’s absence, threatens to vote against Mayor Quimby, and demands the truth about the “Crimson Dawn.”

An unnamed citizen of New Avalon facing mortal danger and the loss of family. This citizen resists surrender, condemns the army’s absence, threatens to vote against Mayor Quimby, and demands the truth about the “Crimson Dawn.”
Fineous is a named figure labeled “Supplies.” He says he has what a visitor needs and offers goods and repairs.
Mayor Quimby is the mayor of New Avalon. Prince Keleseth has ordered his death as part of a plan to infiltrate the town hall, kill its officials and take the New Avalon Registry.
A New Avalon councilman in the New Avalon area.
Scarlet Commander Rodrick is a Scarlet commander in New Avalon.
High Inquisitor Valroth is an inquisitor in New Avalon.
A Scarlet Inquisitor found around New Avalon.
A death knight who tosses torches when not fighting, and in battle uses Icy Touch, Plague Strike and Blood Strike.
A death knight who tosses torches when not fighting.

Malar Bravehorn is a tauren and an Argent Dawn prisoner held by the Crusade. He appeals to a death knight to remember being a champion of the tauren and resist the Lich King's control; he also asks to be put out of his misery.

Olrun the Battlecaller is a death knight of Acherus who directs the rite of Death's Challenge, ordering challengers to duel other death knights. Her instructions invoke victory for the Scourge and glory for the Lich King, placing her in the Scourge's service.

Knight Commander Plaguefist is stationed at the Chapel of the Crimson Flame, where he oversees orders against Argent Dawn prisoners. He describes the prisoners as feisty and singles them out for execution; when the attack inside takes too long, he calls impatiently for an update.

Ellen Stanbridge is an Argent Dawn prisoner held near the Chapel of the Crimson Flame. She remembers being born in Elwynn and once serving as an Alliance champion, and urges the one who comes to execute her to resist the Lich King's control. In anguish, she asks to be put out of her misery.

Yazmina is an Argent Dawn prisoner marked for execution. A kaldorei, she recalls caring for a death knight she recognizes as a child while their mother served at the Temple of the Moon, and calls Teldrassil home. She urges that former champion to resist the Lich King's control before pleading for release through death.

Donovan is an Argent Dawn prisoner marked for execution and a dwarf who identifies himself with Ironforge. He recognizes the listener, asks what has been done to them, and urges them to fight the Lich King's control. As that appeal ends, he asks the listener to put him out of his misery.

Goby Blastenheimer is a gnome who urges a death knight to recall Gnomeregan before the troggs and their former place as a champion of gnome-kind. He urges that person to resist the Lich King’s control and asks to be put out of his misery.

Valok the Righteous is a draenei who urges a death knight to remember being born on Argus and once serving as a champion of their people. He warns that person to resist the Lich King’s control and asks to be put out of his misery; his unfinished plea, “You’ll look me in the eyes when…”, leaves his accusation unsaid.

Antoine Brack is a Forsaken who was human before Lordaeron fell and was freed from Scourge control by the Dark Lady. He remembers fighting the Lich King alongside the Forsaken as a champion. He recognizes the listener as a former ally, urgently urges resistance to the Lich King, and asks for death.

Kug Ironjaw is an orc who recalls Durotar and the Valley of Trials, where the Horde was freed from the blood curse. He remembers being a Horde champion and appeals to a former comrade to resist the Lich King. His dialogue shows a proud orc who would rather die as one than remain a prisoner.

Iggy Darktusk is a troll and an Argent Dawn prisoner held by the Scarlet Crusade. He remembers being a troll hero and “mojo master,” recognizes the one before him as someone he knew before the Scourge took their memories, urges them to resist the Lich King's control, and grieves that it has stripped away their former identity.

Lady Eonys is a blood elf and an Argent Dawn prisoner held by the Scarlet Crusade. Born in Silvermoon, she remembers being a champion of the sin'dorei and urges the one who comes to execute her to fight the Lich King's control. Her pleas turn to despair: she begs to be put out of her misery.

High General Abbendis commands the Scarlet Onslaught at King's Harbor and announces the Scarlet Crusade's transformation into the new force. She is focused on moving Scarlet armies toward Northrend and fears the Scourge will overrun New Avalon and Havenshire. She warns that armies from Hearthglen and Tirisfal must not reach New Avalon, and is alert to courier delays.
High Abbot Landgren is a humanoid in the Scarlet Enclave.
A Scarlet Champion, one of the Scarlet forces' champions in the Scarlet Enclave.
A death knight champion in the Scarlet Enclave, distinct from the Scarlet champions.
A Hearthglen Crusader, one of many found across the Scarlet Enclave.
A Tirisfal Crusader, one of many found across the Scarlet Enclave.

The Scarlet Ballista is a siege weapon whose projectiles threaten targets in its line of fire. The Lich King's campaign against the Scarlet Crusade names ballistas among its specified destruction targets.
A Death Knight Champion is an undead fighter who uses Icy Touch, Plague Strike, Blood Strike, and Death Coil in combat.
Prince Valanar is an undead prince.
Prince Keleseth is an undead prince.
Baron Rivendare is an undead baron.

The Lich King directs the Scourge campaign against the Scarlet forces. At Death's Breach, he addresses a death knight as his champion, orders the Crusade destroyed, and points toward Light's Hope Chapel as the next target. His commands are cold and theatrical: he calls for surrender, threatens to remake crusaders, and presents devastation as a lesson to his enemies.

Gothik the Harvester taunts a captive suspended in slime, mocking their pain and dismissing the idea of sparing them because their civilization has just been eradicated. He draws out the threat of killing them, sounding amused by their helplessness. He is a cruel, self-assured captor.
Noth the Plaguebringer urges his forces to gather more flesh and redouble their efforts, warning that the final assault is near.
An undead volatile ghoul that erupts in a Ghoulplosion when it dies.

Highlord Darion Mograine commands the Scourge attack on the Argent Dawn at Light's Hope, but the Lich King's hold over him is broken there. He then vows that the Knights of the Ebon Blade will fight to end the Lich King and leads their effort to retake Acherus. Darion recalls sacrificing himself to free his father's cursed soul; his words convey grief and resolve.
A volatile ghoul is an undead creature.
A rampaging undead abomination that cleaves in battle.
A Howling Geist is a geist, a hostile creature encountered in the frozen north.
An Acherus Necromancer is a necromancer associated with Acherus.
The Scarlet Deserter is frightened and deeply reluctant, repeatedly asking to be spared or killed instead; as events unfold, they say it tingles before crying, “The horror! THE HORROR!”
A Scourge Gryphon is a gryphon bearing the Scourge designation.
A Scourge Gryphon is a gryphon bearing the Scourge designation.

An Unworthy Initiate, chained at the Heart of Acherus among those deemed unworthy of the dark brotherhood. Set free to fight, it vows to escape this cursed place, despairs of the future, and warns its attacker they have made a grave error.
An Unworthy Initiate who longs to win freedom and leave a cursed place, yet voices despair about the future. When confronted, the initiate answers with a defiant warning.
An Unworthy Initiate who longs to win freedom and leave a cursed place, yet voices despair about the future. When confronted, the initiate answers with a defiant warning.
An Unworthy Initiate who longs to win freedom and leave a cursed place, yet voices despair about the future. When confronted, the initiate answers with a defiant warning.
An Unworthy Initiate who longs to win freedom and leave a cursed place, yet voices despair about the future. When confronted, the initiate answers with a defiant warning.

Scourge Commander Thalanor is a Scourge officer at Browman Mill. He frames the assault on Light's Hope Chapel as a blow against the Argent Dawn that will win Scourge troops a place among immortal heroes, and points those ready for battle to Highlord Darion Mograine, who commands the final march.

place_records.text: You are in Plaguelands: The Scarlet Enclave, a land in the Eastern Kingdoms held by neither the Alliance nor the Horde. Its main settlements are the Crypt of Remembrance and Death's Breach, and neither side holds them. Scarlet Crusade soldiers, miners and land cannons hold parts of the land, while Scourge death knights, ghouls and geists press against them.

You are in New Avalon, a town in the Scarlet Enclave. Thassarian, a Scourge death knight, still hopes that Koltira Deathweaver survived capture by the Scarlet Crusade. Hearthglen and Tirisfal crusaders and Scarlet crusaders patrol the town, and the Scarlet Hold lies northeast of here.

You are in New Avalon Orchard, among the orchards of New Avalon. Orbaz Bloodbane, a calculating Scourge death knight, directs the campaign against the Scarlet Crusade from the Scarlet Tavern behind these orchards, running undercover courier operations. Scarlet marksmen, crusaders and commanders still roam the orchard.

You are in the New Avalon Town Hall, where Mayor Quimby and the town's councilmen work. Prince Keleseth has ordered the mayor killed and the town's registry taken from this building, and the hall is dangerous: Scarlet crusaders and the town's citizens are hostile here.

You are in Havenshire, a settlement in the Scarlet Enclave. Gothik the Harvester, a Scourge figure, examines corpses for what they may yield and curses the geists that interfere with the bodies. Acherus geists and an Acherus necromancer wander here, while Scarlet peasants and shadowy tormentors are the hostile dangers.

You are in Havenshire Farms, a farm in the Scarlet Enclave. Noth the Plaguebringer, a Scourge plague specialist, is building a plague cauldron for New Avalon, a cauldron whose gas is deadly to the living and empowers the Scourge. Scarlet farm hounds and shadowy tormentors roam the fields, and a Scourge plaguehound patrols the grounds.

You are in Havenshire Lumber Mill, a mill in the Scarlet Enclave. Gluttonous geists and volatile ghouls wander the grounds. Scarlet peasants, Scarlet infantrymen and Tirisfal crusaders are the hostile dangers here.

You are in Havenshire Stables, a stable in the Scarlet Enclave where horses are kept for passengers. Havenshire colts and mares carry the passengers who ride them, and an Acherus deathcharger is kept here. Scarlet infantrymen and medics are the hostile dangers nearby.

You are in the Scarlet Hold, the largest building in New Avalon and a Scarlet Crusade keep. Koltira Deathweaver, a badly wounded Scourge death knight, is held here and urges others to strike back and free the prisoners. High Inquisitor Valroth, Scarlet Commander Rodrick and their crusaders make it dangerous, and the alarms have been raised.

You are in the Chapel of the Crimson Flame, a Scarlet chapel west of New Avalon. Knight Commander Plaguefist oversees the Argent Dawn prisoners held in the nearby prison house and singles them out for execution. Ellen Stanbridge and Malar Bravehorn ask to be put out of their misery, and Scarlet inquisitors and crusaders defend the chapel.
You are in Light's Point Tower, a Scarlet stronghold in the Scarlet Enclave. Scarlet land cannons and fleet guardians are posted here, and scarlet miners are among the hostile creatures nearby.

You are in Light's Point, an area of the Scarlet Enclave. Scarlet fleet defenders gather here in great numbers, and scarlet land cannons and fleet guardians add to the danger. A plague spreader, a Scarlet cannon and an Acherus necromancer are among its people.

You are in the Crypt of Remembrance, a Scourge necropolis in the Scarlet Enclave. Baron Rivendare directs Scourge attacks on New Avalon from here and enjoys the recurring battles with the Crusade. Prince Keleseth, the blood lord who serves the Lich King, uses persuaders to extract information from Scarlet soldiers, and Fineous sells goods and repairs.

You are in Death's Breach, a staging point for Scourge attacks in the Scarlet Enclave. Neither side holds it, and Prince Valanar directs the Scourge campaign against the Scarlet Crusade from here. Gryphons bring arriving death knights in, arranged by Scourge Commander Thalanor from Ebon Hold. Scarlet Crusade prisoners and infantrymen are about, and the place has repairs, a spirit healer and a vendor.

You are in The Noxious Glade, part of the Scarlet Enclave. Gothik the Harvester taunts a captive suspended in slime, and Noth the Plaguebringer urges his forces to gather more flesh, warning that a final assault is near. Undead ghouls and abominations are among those here.
You are in King's Harbor in the Scarlet Enclave. Scarlet Champions are about in large numbers, and Captain Shely and Bishop Street are among those about.
You are in Scarlet Overlook in the Scarlet Enclave. Tirisfal Crusaders, Scarlet Preachers and Scarlet Marksmen are about, and Scarlet ballistae are here too.

You are in Light's Hope Chapel in the Scarlet Enclave, where the Argent Dawn stands against the Scourge. A spirit healer here offers a return to life for a price, though it may not yet be the traveler's time.

You are in Browman Mill in the Scarlet Enclave. Scourge Commander Thalanor is a Scourge officer here, and Highlord Darion Mograine, freed of the Lich King's hold at Light's Hope, leads the Knights of the Ebon Blade in an effort to retake Acherus.
You are in Havenshire Mine in the Scarlet Enclave. Scarlet miners, peasants and infantrymen are about the workings, and a Gluttonous Geist, an undead creature, is here too.

You are in The Noxious Pass in the Scarlet Enclave, where death knights are trained. Instructor Razuvious teaches runeforging, and Lord Thorval is headmaster of the blood school in the Hall of Command, one of three dark arts taught there. Newly raised Death Knight Initiates are among the people here.
